transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I came in today because... I just can't seem to shake this feeling I've been having. Even on my better days, it feels like some of the people at my church, and in my walking club, are watching me. 

It's a bit hard to explain, but it seems like they're putting little messages about me in the church bulletin, or slipping things about me into what they say when we're all together. It's just been really bothering me, so I thought I should come in and talk to someone about it.
How long have you been noticing these feelings that people are watching you or sending hidden messages about you?

Well, it's been a while. I'd say the messages... and also some voices I've been hearing, along with just having trouble keeping my thoughts straight... all of that has been happening for about eleven months now.

During these past eleven months, have you also had periods where you felt extremely sad, hopeless, or lost interest in things, or alternatively periods where you felt unusually elated, energetic, or needed little sleep?

Yes, I have. I haven't really had any times where I felt overly energetic or anything like that, but I've definitely had some very low periods. 

There was a stretch where I felt incredibly sad and just... hopeless. I lost interest in pretty much everything. I was barely eating, and I just kept thinking that I had failed everyone in my life. And the thing is, even when I was at my absolute lowest like that, I was still hearing my friend's voice and believing that the people at church were putting those messages about me in the bulletin. It didn't stop just because I was feeling so down.

Outside of that low, depressive period you described, was there a time—lasting at least a couple of weeks—when you were not feeling depressed at all, but still heard the voice or believed people were sending messages about you?

Yes, there was. Um, maybe a few months ago, I had a spell that lasted for several weeks where I actually felt okay. I was getting dressed every day, eating a bit better, and I just didn't feel so... weighed down by that sadness. But even during those weeks when I wasn't feeling depressed, I was still hearing my name being called in the house, and I still thought the people at church were dropping hints about me. So, yes, that part didn't go away even when my mood lifted.

latest_inference.note: Confirmed psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations, delusions of reference) persisted during a period of at least several weeks with no depressive symptoms, satisfying the requirement that psychotic symptoms occur independent of mood episodes. Combined with a clear major depressive episode overlapping with psychosis, this fits schizoaffective disorder, depressive type (F25.1) rather than unspecified schizoaffective disorder or schizophrenia alone.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports psychotic symptoms (persecutory and referential delusions about church/walking club, auditory hallucinations, disorganized thinking) persisting for about 11 months. During this period, she experienced a major depressive episode (depressed mood, anhedonia, poor appetite, guilt/worthlessness) concurrent with the psychotic symptoms, satisfying Criterion A for a mood episode co-occurring with active-phase psychotic symptoms. Critically, she also had a distinct period lasting several weeks where her mood was euthymic (no depressive symptoms) but the delusions and hallucinations persisted, fulfilling Criterion B (psychotic symptoms present for at least 2 weeks in the absence of a mood episode). Since the depressive episode has been present for a substantial portion of the total illness duration and no manic/hypomanic symptoms were reported, this best fits Schizoaffective Disorder, Depressive Type (F25.1), rather than Schizophrenia (which would require absence of a prominent mood component) or Major Depressive Disorder with psychotic features (which would not allow psychosis to persist independently of mood episodes for 2+ weeks).
